Use the `--workers` option when you start the app with the `fastapi` command. If you have more clients than what a single process can handle (for example if the virtual machine is not too big) and you have **multiple cores** in the server's CPU, then you could have **multiple processes** running with the same application at the same time, and distribute all the requests among them.[5]

```console
$ fastapi run --workers 4 main.py
```

With this setup, one Uvicorn **process manager** would listen on the **IP** and **port**, and it would start **multiple Uvicorn worker processes**.[3]

**Things to keep in mind:**

- **Memory:** Multiple processes normally **don't share any memory**.[2] For example, if your app loads a 1 GB model, if you start **4 processes** (4 workers), each will consume 1 GB of RAM. So in total, your API will consume **4 GB of RAM**.[2]
- **Docker:** In a Dockerfile, add the option to the command: `CMD ["fastapi", "run", "app/main.py", "--port", "80", "--workers", "4"]`[1]
- **Clusters such as Kubernetes:** If the cluster already handles replication, you **would not** want to have multiple workers in the container, for example with the `--workers` command line option. You would want to have just a **single Uvicorn process** per container (but probably multiple containers).[1]
